text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAILY TIMES
- Former finance minister Olu Falae and nine other people may be charged over bomb blasts in Nigeria, sources say.
- Population of Nigeria from 1991 census stands at 88.9 million; final report submitted to military ruler General Sani Abacha in the capital Abuja.
- A local private telecommunications firm, NITTI, says it plans to provide one million telephone lines nationwide.

- ADC airline's plane crash in November which killed all 143 on board was caused by human error, says aviation minister Air Commodore Ita Udo-Imeh as he receives report of an investigation into the disaster.
THE GUARDIAN

- Civil servants now to retire at age of 60 irrespective of length of service unlike previously when they quit at 60 or after 35 years whichever came first, according to new regulations just published.
- Associates of Michael Ajasin, 88-year-old leader of opposition NADECO group, dispel speculation that his health is failing following his latest admission to hospital.
- Twelve human rights groups file court suit to stop the military government from publishing or enacting a new constitution for the country.
- Nigeria earned 24 billion naira last year from export of agricultural produce compared with 21 billion the year before.
- Demand at weekly foreign exchange auction rises to $86.3 million this week from $83.5 million last week.
- Nigerian Maritime Authority, regulator of shipping business, says dishonest firms will lose their licences.
- National carrier Nigeria Airways suspends four staff over controversial aircraft maintenance deal.
THISDAY
- A senior Nigerian executive of Shell calls for sustainable investment in the oil sector.
- The discovery of an object suspected to be a bomb causes pandemonium at a power sub-station in oil city of Port Harcourt.
- Lagos court to rule on March 5 on whether to issue a warrant for detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola to be brought to court to testify in suit challenging his detention.
